mechanism: Fluoxetine enhances central serotonergic activity while scopolamine has anticholinergic properties; additive CNS depression and anticholinergic effects may occur, with potential serotonin syndrome risk at higher doses.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion) and CNS depression; consider alternative antiemetic if clinically feasible, or use lowest effective scopolamine dose with careful patient observation.
